theorem.endpoint: The endpoint-uniform theorem gives the single projective endpoint [0:1] for the same separated supports and nonzero weights.
theorem.finite_root_bound: By the low-degree transfer, every finite ambient root is represented by a projective auxiliary polynomial Q with deg Q<h.  At A=387, h=1, so the projective Q-space is a single point.
theorem.projective_safety: The support-wise projective total is at most one finite split-locator slope plus the endpoint, hence <=2<=6.
theorem.split_locator_bound: The null-polynomial split-locator gate can only remove finite ambient roots, so the finite support-wise split-locator count is also at most one.
theorem.unique_slope_bound: For the single Q-class, the six direction-node equations either are inconsistent or determine one scalar z.  Hence there is at most one finite ambient root.
